data.name: Ziro
data.detailed_description:
Once upon a time The Earth was green and beautiful. It was entrusted to humans to use it wisely together with all living things.
Over time humans developed advanced technology using up the Earth’s natural resources. Humans lost their connection with the Earth. Caring only for their selfish interests, they didn’t notice the injuries that they had inflicted upon the Earth.
Climate change became the Earth’s scream for help. But nobody heard. Nobody until the cries become so strong that they woke up Ziro, the youngest member of the ancient order of Snowmen Earth guardians.
Ziro will take you on a journey of puzzle solving. You will be able to learn how you can reconnect and help Mother Earth.
Ziro is innovative puzzle game offering incredible game-play in various levels of difficulty. You can relax and enjoy, or try to solve a serious puzzle that will prove to be a true challenge even for the experienced puzzle solver.
So, Warm Up The Brain and Cool Down The Earth!
Key features:
  • Puzzle game featuring over 300 mind-cracking levels that will take player all around world in noble quest of fighting global warming
  • Full 3D graphics powered by Ultra Engine technology that provides stunning graphics and visual effects rarely seen in casual games
  • A wide variety of puzzle elements that will heat up even the most prepared brains
  • Relax tension of problem solving and boost up your mood with 40 minutes of funky music
  • 3 different game modes: Quest, Skill and Practice – a challenge for everyone’s taste
  • 36 Steam Achievements
  • Each level Leaderboard, including total Leaderboards for each game mode
  • Enjoy the trip around the world through beautiful environments that are unique and characteristic for each part of the globe
  • Learn the most important facts about global warming through fun and excitement

reviews.review:
Ziro is a colorful puzzle title from developer Kokakiki and publisher Kalypso Media Digital that arrived during a period when casual puzzle games were flourishing on PC. Rather than focusing solely on abstract challenges, the game builds its identity around an environmental narrative, casting players as a young snowman entrusted with helping restore balance to a planet suffering from the effects of climate change. It is an unusual premise that gives the game a distinctive personality, even if its storytelling remains relatively light throughout the experience.

The heart of Ziro lies in its extensive collection of puzzles. With more than 300 stages to complete, the game offers a considerable amount of content for fans of the genre. Its mechanics are easy enough to understand at first, but the complexity increases steadily as new elements are introduced. Early levels serve as a gentle introduction, while later challenges demand patience, strategy, and careful observation. The game avoids becoming entirely repetitive by introducing fresh twists over time, though some players may still feel the weight of its lengthy campaign during extended sessions.

One of Ziro's greatest strengths is the variety of ways it allows players to engage with its puzzles. Quest Mode provides a structured journey across different regions, while Skill Mode caters to those seeking tougher challenges and higher scores. Practice Mode rounds out the package by giving players an opportunity to experiment without the pressure of progression. The inclusion of online leaderboards and numerous achievements adds an extra incentive for completionists, encouraging players to revisit levels in pursuit of better performances.

From a presentation standpoint, Ziro embraces a bright and playful visual style. Its environments are vibrant and diverse enough to keep the adventure visually engaging despite the game's age. The titular protagonist is simple yet memorable, and the overall aesthetic fits the family-friendly tone of the experience. While modern audiences will immediately recognize the limitations of a title released in 2010, there is still a certain charm in its colorful art direction that helps it stand apart from more generic puzzle offerings of its era.

The soundtrack complements the gameplay effectively, featuring upbeat tunes that maintain a relaxing atmosphere even when the puzzles become frustratingly difficult. Audio design is not particularly groundbreaking, but it succeeds in supporting the game's lighthearted tone. Combined with its accessible system requirements, Ziro remains an easy title to pick up and play on a wide range of hardware, making it a convenient choice for players looking for a casual experience without demanding technical specifications.

However, the game is not without its flaws. Its environmental message feels more like a thematic backdrop than an integral component of the gameplay, and some players may find the connection between the narrative and the puzzles somewhat superficial. Additionally, the user interface and certain gameplay elements have not aged gracefully, resulting in occasional moments of frustration. The difficulty curve can also be uneven, with some levels presenting abrupt spikes that may discourage less experienced puzzle fans.

Despite these shortcomings, Ziro succeeds as an ambitious puzzle game with a unique identity. Its substantial amount of content, varied game modes, and charming presentation make it an enjoyable experience for players who appreciate old-school puzzle design. While it may not leave a lasting impact on the genre, it remains a worthwhile curiosity that demonstrates how even a simple puzzle game can attempt to deliver a message alongside its gameplay.

Rating: 6/10
